claims.text: An interpretability-enhanced machine-learning model can accurately predict low phonon thermal conductivity in single-phase Co–Cr–Fe–Mn–Ni high-entropy alloys.
Lattice-distortion measures, electron-density variation, and phase-stability metrics are relevant descriptors for the proposed model.
The proposed high-dimensional descriptors capture complex atomic-scale disorder.
The model will predict thermal conductivity within 10% of experimental values.
The model will improve predictive accuracy by at least 20% over conventional empirical models.
Binary-alloy data can be used to train a model that performs inference on multielement alloys.
Phase-stability descriptors can be derived using quantities such as electronegativity, valence electron concentration, and CALPHAD-derived information.
The model is applicable from room temperature to approximately 1200 °C for samples whose phase stability is preserved.
Atomic-scale chemical disorder enhances phonon scattering.
Maintained phase homogeneity enhances phonon scattering.
Increased lattice distortion and related disorder lower the phonon mean free path.
A lower phonon mean free path reduces effective thermal conductivity.
Incorporating the proposed mechanistic descriptors produces more accurate predictions than additive empirical models.
Conventional empirical or rule-of-mixtures models typically deviate by more than 10% from experimental HEA thermal-conductivity values.
The approach is limited to single-phase solid-solution HEAs without significant intermetallic precipitates.
The model's validity is confined to the compositional and processing spaces represented in its training data.
The approach may not extrapolate to alloys with substantial phase segregation or complex multiphase microstructures.
The magnitude of the accuracy improvement depends on the representativeness and quality of the HEA-specific experimental data.
